title: A colleague takes credit for your work
situation: In a meeting, a teammate presents your idea as theirs. Everyone nods. You're furious.

advice.say: Don't call them a liar in public. Ask a curious question about the details only you would know, and let the room see who really did the work.
Make your work visible from now on: share progress early and often, so nobody can quietly borrow it again.
Don't let anger turn this into a feud. Calm firmness wins more than a fight.

title: You keep putting off something important
situation: The course, the gym, the call you need to make. It's been 'next week' for months.

advice.say: You're busy, but life isn't waiting. The 'right time' never comes.
Count how long you've already delayed. That number is the argument for today.
Act on the decision the very first chance you get, even in a tiny way, before the feeling fades.

title: Someone insults you in front of others
situation: A sharp remark, people laugh, and your face goes hot.

advice.say: They said it because it seemed right to them. Their mistake hurts them, not you.
Answer with calm, not a counter-insult. Anger met with anger only grows.
Be decent to them later. Kindness they didn't earn is the punishment they'll remember.

title: You're nervous about a presentation
situation: Tomorrow you speak in front of the class or team, and your stomach is already in knots.

advice.say: Confidence comes from preparation. Know your material so well there's nothing left to fear.
Rehearse out loud, again and again. Like horses used to trains, you'll stop flinching.
Do the talk well and let go of how it's received. The effort is yours; the applause isn't.

title: Your boss asks what you think of their bad idea
situation: They're excited. You can see three problems.

advice.say: Don't make them look foolish. Let them keep the credit for the good parts.
Skip 'you're wrong'. Try 'I wonder if…' and let them discover the flaw themselves.
A wise leader wants the truth. If yours punishes honesty, you've learned something important about them.

title: A friend keeps borrowing money and never pays it back
situation: Small amounts, always a good story, never returned.

advice.say: Money changes how people treat each other. Notice whether the friendship lives without it.
Endless generosity drains you and earns resentment, not gratitude. It's okay to stop.
Watch what they want, not what they say. Self-interest can wear any face.

title: You lost something you cared about
situation: A job, a relationship, a chance you were sure of.

advice.say: Say 'it has been returned', not 'I lost it'. It was never fully yours to keep.
Everything changes; this will too. The pain is real, and so is the change still coming.
You're never quite as unhappy as you feel right now. Give it time.

title: You want to build a new habit
situation: Gym, reading, waking early: you start strong and fade by week two.

advice.say: Allow no exceptions until it's rooted. Every skipped day undoes several good ones.
Track it. Franklin kept a page per virtue and marked every slip.
Start tiny. A thousand-mile journey still begins with one step.

title: Everyone around you is doing something you think is wrong
situation: The group chat, the team, the friends. Going along is easier.

advice.say: In a crowd, good people do what they never would alone. Notice when it's happening to you.
To be yourself you sometimes have to stand apart.
Madness is rare in one person and normal in groups. The group being sure proves nothing.

title: You're leading a team for the first time
situation: You were one of them yesterday. Now you're in charge.

advice.say: Be kind first, then firm. Humanity earns loyalty; discipline keeps it.
Put yourself last. The leader who serves ends up in front.
Your success is their wellbeing. When the team thrives, so do you.

title: A rival is trying to provoke you
situation: They needle you, hoping you'll snap in front of everyone.

advice.say: Never act out of anger. That's exactly what they want.
Stay calm and let them be the one who loses their temper.
A bitter cucumber? Put it down. Brambles? Walk around. Not every thorn needs a fight.

title: Safe path or risky dream?
situation: A stable option on one side, the thing you really want on the other.

advice.say: Fortune favours the bold more than the cautious.
Your own path done imperfectly beats someone else's done well.
Trust yourself. Every heart answers to that string.

title: Your plan failed and you blame bad luck
situation: You did everything right, you think, and it still fell apart.

advice.say: People don't prepare in calm weather. Next time, build the dykes before the flood.
Circumstances don't make you; they show you who you are. What did this one show?
Luck needs effort. Even the lion has to hunt.

title: You want to win an argument
situation: You know you're right and you want them to admit it.

advice.say: Ask questions like a curious beginner. People accept what they think they discovered.
Hard words when kind ones work is like choosing unripe fruit.
The best victory needs no battle. Win the person, not the argument.
